title: Dark radiation from Kerr primordial black holes: the role of superradiance
summary: Light primordial black holes (PBHs) that fully evaporate before Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) produce dark radiation (DR) via Hawking radiation of gravitons, contributing to the effective number of relativistic species $ΔN_{\rm eff}$. If the particle spectrum contains a beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) boson with Compton wavelength comparable to the black hole (BH) gravitational radius, superradiant instability extracts angular momentum from the BH into a bosonic cloud, whose gravitational wave (GW) emission contributes an additional source of DR.
